Thanks for the quick onboarding invite. Attaching Kopano's VAT registration and company registration extract for South Africa. A couple of specifics we need to confirm before we proceed with the first PO: 

- Will Redwood accept invoices from Kopano (ZA) gross with SA VAT, or will Redwood apply reverse-charge (no VAT on our side) and require a fiscal representative?
- Our bank is local; do you need a separate remittance instruction for Redwood's EU buying entity or can payments go to the ZA bank account and Redwood handle entity-level PO split?

Attachments: Kopano_TaxCertificate_ZA.pdf (VAT reg), Kopano_Company_Reg_2027.pdf (CIPC extract)

We can also provide a local fiscal rep if required — we have an appointed agent for EU/UK clients. Please advise the exact fields you need on the invoice and the preferred PO entity so we can configure our billing system.

Regards,

Hi Marius — thanks for sending these. Quick checklist and next steps from procurement/finance so we can complete vendor setup and issue POs: 

1) Vendor documents we need in final PDF (you already sent some):
   - South Africa VAT registration certificate (copy) — received
   - Company registration (CIPC) — received
   - Official invoice sample showing where VAT is reported (if you have one)
   - Copy of a signed remittance instruction / bank confirmation (for cross-border payments)

2) Tax/treatment questions (please confirm):
   - Do Kopano invoices include VAT line for services to a foreign principal, or do you currently zero-rate exports?
   - If you do charge VAT to a foreign customer, confirm whether Kopano can issue an invoice excluding VAT when the customer provides a valid foreign VAT registration/ID.

3) PO routing & entity split:
   - Redwood prefers to map POs to the legal buying entity that will be charged. For now, please provide the billing country you want us to target (ZA bank vs EU entity). If you want invoices routed to Redwood's EU entity, we'll need to issue a PO to Redwood EU and provide the EU billing contact.

Finance (cc Ben) — can you confirm whether Redwood requires a fiscal representative for ZA suppliers or if reverse-charge handling is the recommended path for our contracting model?

I'll hold off issuing the first PO until we confirm the above.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marius van der Merwe <mvdm@kopano.co.za>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding docs — Kopano (ZA) VAT cert + PO routing question

Thanks — quick finance notes (internal and for Marius):

- South Africa VAT reverse charge rules: for inbound services to a SA entity, VAT is charged; for services supplied by a SA vendor to a foreign recipient, SA VAT can be zero-rated if export criteria are met. Because Redwood will be billed from a non-ZA legal entity in many cases, we typically request invoices without SA VAT and collect evidence (proof of export, contract with a non-SA buyer).

- Redwood does not require Kopano to appoint a SA fiscal representative for normal B2B services if Kopano is the supplier charging VAT. The fiscal representative usually applies where a non-resident is required to register. If Kopano is registered in ZA (you have VAT reg #), you can issue invoices in ZA and we can handle the PO mapping.

- Preferred flow for minimal friction: Kopano issues invoices to "Redwood EU" (specifically: Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd, VAT ID: GB999999999) if they want payment from our EU buying entity. Alternatively, if Kopano prefers to be paid in ZA, Redwood can issue the PO to Redwood (US) but run an intercompany cost allocation to the proper entity; that adds a minor accounting step on our side.

Action items for Kopano:
  a) Confirm whether your invoices to Redwood will include SA VAT or be zero-rated.
  b) If you prefer Redwood to pay Kopano's ZA bank account, please provide remittance instructions and confirm currency (ZAR).
  c) If you want to bill Redwood EU, confirm you can invoice to the EU entity and collect EU billing contact info below.

Laura — can you share the sample PO mapping template so Kopano can see how we split cost center / legal entity fields? (Attaching a sample workbook in thread.)

- Ben Carter
Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Marius van der Merwe <mvdm@kopano.co.za>

Hi Neha / Ben / Laura,

Thanks for the clarifications — we prefer the simplest path to get the first PO through. Answers below: 

1) Kopano will issue invoices to Redwood EU (Redwood Inference EMEA Ltd) and can omit SA VAT on those invoices — we'll include an export note and attach the transport/contract evidence where required.

2) Bank instructions: we are happy to receive payments to our ZA account for local currency settlements, but for Redwood EU payments we can also raise invoices to the EU entity and provide an IBAN. Please find attached a signed remittance instruction for the ZA bank account.

3) Fiscal rep: not necessary — Kopano is VAT-registered in SA and will manage VAT filings locally.

I've attached the remittance confirmation and a sample invoice with the invoice fields you requested. Please confirm the Redwood billing entity (EU or US) and the exact PO fields so we can match.

Attachments: PO-Entity-Mapping_Sample.xlsx (sample showing Redwood fields), Kopano_TaxCertificate_ZA.pdf (resend)

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you prefer to finalise the mapping.

Best,
Marius
Kopano Logistics
